main_text.p: commeatus sufficiebant ; demum jus habebant usurpabantve tum praemiis honorandi, tum poenis afficiendi quos & quando volebant, à magistratibus quoque omnibus rationes exigendi, & eosdem, atque adeò ipsos reges, si colli-beret, imperio exuendi, in carcerem compingendi, capitis denique arcessen-di, damnandique: ut non sine ratione Plato & Aristoteles scripsisse videantur, speciem tyrannidis potestatem ephoro-rum apud Spartanos habere. Sed moderamen in eo hoc erat, quòd potestas tantum esset annua, & quòd, cum numero quinque essent ephori, si quid iniqui pararent eorum duo, reliquorum trium dissensione aut intercessione a-verti id posset. Nam singuli potestatem non habebant, sed ea penes collegium erat: in eo verò id valebat, quod plurium suffragiis decernebatur. Porrò cum ephoris magistratibus ineuntibus annum quoque suum Lacedaemonii inchoabant. Et ex Aristotele affirmat Plutarchus, ephoros initio muneris sui vo-ce praeconis praecepisse omnibus civibus, ut labii superioris pilos ponerent, & le-tibus mentem adverterent, ne ipsi necessum haberent in eos animadverte-re. Quorum prius ad obsequium etiam in minimis promptè praestandum per-tinuisse,

page.notes: Left edge: stray marks and faint strokes at the scan edge (for example near "ut labii" and "le-tibus") are scan edge or show-through, not text; the line "ut labii superioris" is read from the lines and marked as read, with "vt" printed as "vt" and changed to "ut". Bottom left: a small faint mark (possibly a gathering signature, roughly "ɨL" or "iL"), too unclear to read, so omitted. Printed long s and ligature forms (s, ff, ffi) were transcribed as plain s and ss; "eflet" and "eflent" are read as printed, and their spelling was normalised to esset and essent. No doubtful words on this page.
